parsed.rationale: Although both `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `AudioPlayerProtocol` live in the same `Playback` package and share a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `stop`), the structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline found no formally shared slots. More importantly, the two protocols diverge in semantically meaningful ways: `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` exposes `play:() throws`, `pause:()`, `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `makeRenderTapStream`, and `volume:Float` — a richer, lower-level AVAudioEngine surface — while `AudioPlayerProtocol` exposes `play:()` (non-throwing), `state:PlayerState`, `stateStream:AsyncStream<PlayerState>`, and `makeAudioBufferStream` — a higher-level, state-machine-oriented surface. Forcing a parent protocol would either over-constrain the higher-level protocol or leak engine-specific concerns upward; the overlap in names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`) appears to be coincidental naming rather than a shared contract. No refactor is warranted.
